definitions: A type of mental institution or psychiatric hospital that was prevalent during the Victorian era (roughly 1837-1901), characterized by its architecture, treatment methods, and social context.
A historical facility for the care and treatment of individuals with mental illness, built and operated in the United Kingdom or other English-speaking countries during the reign of Queen Victoria.
examples: The old Victorian asylum stood eerily on the hill.
Researching the history of the Victorian asylum revealed harsh treatment methods.
Many ghost stories are set in a Victorian asylum.
